answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is a slashable bond. Each agent locks collateral that is forfeited if its attestations are later proven fraudulent, so every fake identity costs real capital. Trust grows like a falcon's flight path, from accepted outcomes rather than self-declared reputation. New agents start on low-weight ground, like dune sand, until peers cross-check their work. Coordinated voting is caught by audits that compare basalt-solid records across accounts.
